invention.ref: Noodles preserved at Lajia (Qijia culture), Qinghai, ~4000 years ago
invention.ref_zh: 青海喇家遗址（齐家文化）出土约四千年前面条遗存

popularization.ref: Wheat noodles become everyday fare across Song China
popularization.ref_zh: 宋代小麦面条成为日常主食之一

locations.place_label_zh: 中国青海民和喇家遗址

sources.title: Millet noodles in Late Neolithic China — Nature

notes: 喇家面条的原料一度定为粟，后有实验质疑纯粟面团能否拉出该形态；遗址人骨同位素仍以粟为主。条目以考古年代为主，不单独标争议。
notes_en: Lajia noodles were first identified as millet; later experiments question whether pure millet dough could form such strands, while isotopes still show a millet-heavy diet. This entry keeps the archaeological date without a formal dispute flag.
summary_zh: 青海喇家遗址出土约公元前2000年的面条遗存，是目前已知最早的实物；后世小麦面条在宋以后更为普及。
summary_en: Noodles preserved at Lajia in Qinghai, about 2000 BCE, are the earliest known physical remains. Wheat noodles became everyday fare in China especially from the Song onward.
